tldr: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro surfaced after Arena testing on Oct 23 and launched Oct 24 as a roughly 3T-parameter API flagship, then a botched launch forced a quota reset and apology. The Hugging Face listing appeared Nov 2, full 1.56TB weights were reported Nov 5, and vLLM, Huawei Ascend and Moore Threads added serving and fine-tuning support.
whats_new: A Kimi K3.1 Pro Coder variant has arrived at 775 GB and is reported to fit on one GPU, about half the size of the 1.56TB full checkpoint.
why_it_matters: A coding-focused 775 GB variant lowers the hardware bar for self-hosting a frontier-class open-weight coder, while the full Pro model still needs a large multi-accelerator cluster.

status.detail: Weights are public with conditional commercial use, engine and accelerator support is spreading, and a smaller Coder variant now targets single-GPU deployment.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 appears after Arena testing and is compared to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro as its new flagship
beats.summary: Coverage describes a roughly 3T-parameter model and a faster Highspeed API tier.

beats.headline: User quota complaints force a reset and an apology
beats.summary: Moonshot reset Kimi K3.1 Pro quotas, then publicly apologised for the botched launch and restored user quotas.

beats.headline: Third-party platforms add Kimi K3.1 Pro
beats.summary: NEAR AI Cloud, ZenMux and Verda Inference list it, and vLLM ships day-0 support.

beats.headline: Moonshot releases full Kimi K3.1 Pro weights
beats.summary: The Hugging Face listing appeared Nov 2; reports on Nov 5 cite free 1.56TB weights with commercial use permitted under conditions.

beats.headline: Training and domestic-hardware support forms around the weights
beats.summary: vLLM covers zero-mismatch async RL with Kimi K3.1, Moore Threads adds day-zero serving, and Huawei Ascend adapts it for LoRA fine-tuning.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro Coder ships at 775 GB, pitched to fit one GPU

open_questions: What are the exact commercial-use conditions in the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights license, and do they cover the Coder variant?
What quantization or architecture change lets the 775 GB Coder fit on one GPU, and which GPU is required?
Do independent coding benchmarks show how much quality the Coder variant gives up against the full Pro model?
Will Moonshot's hosted API quotas and the Highspeed tier stay stable after the launch reset?
Which serving stacks beyond vLLM and Ascend publish production-ready Kimi K3.1 Pro recipes?
take_for_builders: If you want a self-hosted open-weight coding model, evaluate the 775 GB Coder variant on your own coding evals before sizing a cluster for the 1.56TB Pro, and check the license conditions first.
